pointers.sentence: Since 6.0 it builds an `email.message.EmailMessage` under a policy, `email.policy.default` unless its new policy argument names another, and the policy does the checking (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.message`).
The new value has the old classes' API but is no instance of them, the 6.0 notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

A newline in the subject raised Django's `BadHeaderError` under 5.2.17, and raises the policy's `ValueError` since 6.0; `BadHeaderError`, deprecated, is now `ValueError` itself, so that code catching it catches the policy's error (`django/core/mail/message.py:BadHeaderError`).
Importing `BadHeaderError`, `SafeMIMEText` or `SafeMIMEMultipart` from `django.core.mail` warns (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:__getattr__`).

`EmailMessage.attach` takes an `email.message.MIMEPart` since 6.0, which 5.2.17 refused, and attaches a legacy `email.mime.base.MIMEBase` with a warning (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.attach`).
A positional use still works, and warns (`django/utils/deprecation.py:deprecate_posargs`).

Django never used the names, the 6.0 notes say, and since 6.0 both are lists of address strings: as `mail_admins` or `mail_managers` sends, a list of pairs is reduced to its addresses with a warning, and a value that is neither empty nor a list or tuple of strings is `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).

Since 6.1 `MAILERS` names backends by alias, for "configuring multiple email backends with different options" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), and its handler, `django.core.mail.mailers`, makes at each lookup a new backend from an entry's `"BACKEND"` and `"OPTIONS"` (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).

Since 6.1 `MAILERS` names backends by alias, for "configuring multiple email backends with different options" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), and its handler, `django.core.mail.mailers`, makes at each lookup a new backend from an entry's `"BACKEND"` and `"OPTIONS"` (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).
`send_mail` builds an `EmailMultiAlternatives`, and given neither `using=` nor `connection=` hands it the backend `get_connection` makes (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`).

An alias `MAILERS` lacks, or any but `"default"` without it, raises the exception `MailerDoesNotExist`; beside `MAILERS`, `get_connection` makes the `"default"` mailer, its keyword arguments added to the entry's `"OPTIONS"`, unknown ones ignored, and refuses a backend's path with `RuntimeError` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

Without `MAILERS`, `get_connection` makes the backend whose path it is given, or else the class `EMAIL_BACKEND` names, and `mailers` answers `"default"` with it; it warns "Django 2028 will not have a default mailer. …" unless an old email setting is defined, since such a setting warns of its own (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:warn_about_default_mailers_if_needed`, `django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

Without `MAILERS`, `get_connection` makes the backend whose path it is given, or else the class `EMAIL_BACKEND` names, and `mailers` answers `"default"` with it; it warns "Django 2028 will not have a default mailer. …" unless an old email setting is defined, since such a setting warns of its own (`django/core/mail/deprecation.py:warn_about_default_mailers_if_needed`, `django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).
`get_connection` is deprecated (6.1); 5.2.17 and 6.0.8, which knew no `MAILERS`, made the backend of `EMAIL_BACKEND` whatever `MAILERS` held (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

Deprecated with it, and warning only when called from outside Django: connection= and `EmailMessage.connection`, fail_silently=, auth_user= and auth_password= (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).
Here `send_mail` is given a backend as connection= and fail_silently=True; older versions ignored fail_silently= beside a connection, the documentation says (`docs/topics/email.txt`):

Since 6.1 the call is refused before a message is made, after two warnings, of fail_silently= and connection=, whose one class the line names once (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`); credentials beside a connection are refused alike.
A subclass that defines a method get_connection, which `send` called before 6.1, now makes `send` raise `AttributeError` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).
A backend made directly, by calling its class, has the alias `None` and still ignores the argument, with a warning (`django/core/mail/backends/base.py:BaseEmailBackend.__init__`).
An SMTP backend made directly, deprecated too, reads the old settings for what it is not given (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.__init__`).

Where `MAILERS` is defined none can be read, even one left at its default, so given only a host the backend raises `AttributeError` as it reads `EMAIL_PORT`, where 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 read port 25 (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

Its undocumented connection method is no longer called, the 6.1 notes say, and since 6.1 a subclass that defines one raises `AttributeError` as it is made (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.__init__`; [Logging](../startup/logging.md)).
`BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware` takes its alias from `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.using` (`django/middleware/common.py:BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.send_mail`).

Without it, the handler and the middleware send with fail_silently=True, so the SMTP backend passes over a server it cannot reach; with it, they catch only `MailerDoesNotExist`, and unless the mailer's `"OPTIONS"` set `"fail_silently"`, an error in sending is raised from `AdminEmailHandler.emit` to the code that logged the record, since logging does not catch what a handler raises (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.send_mail`).

Since 6.0 the `task` decorator turns a module-level function into a `Task`, and `Task.enqueue` hands it and its arguments to its backend of `TASKS`, which returns a `TaskResult` (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.enqueue`).
Django "does not provide a worker mechanism to run tasks", the 6.0 notes say (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`; [Background tasks: `Task`, `TaskResult` and the task backends](../services/tasks.md)).

Since 6.1 the decorator passes a keyword argument it does not name, run_after apart, to the backend's `BaseTaskBackend.task_class`, where 6.0.8's decorator refused it; the default class, `Task`, takes only its own fields (`django/tasks/base.py:task`).
Since 6.1 `Task.__reduce__` pickles the function's dotted path, and `Task._reconstruct` takes the function from the task bound there (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.__reduce__`).
